title: Tobacco group Imperial Brands to axe up to 4,600 jobs as it uses more AI
html:
Imperial Brands, the owner of Davidoff cigarettes and Blu vapes, is cutting up to 4,600 jobs in a huge cost-saving drive as it uses more AI and other technologies.

The Bristol-based company said this year 2,100 roles would go globally, and it plans a further reduction of between 2,100 and 2,500 jobs by the end of 2030.

Imperial Brands, which has a global workforce of about 25,000 people, will close its Langenhagen factory in Germany next year and has sold a plant in Taiwan, leading to 700 job losses. It is holding consultations on the planned reductions in several countries. The current cuts affect a small number of jobs in the UK.

Lukas Paravicini, the chief executive, said the cuts were part of a “transformation” of the company, with at least £320m of annual savings targeted by 2030.

“We continue to perform and transform,” he said. “We want to become more agile, more data-led, more consumer-facing and more efficient.”

He added: “We’re fusing the organisation with more technologies,” including new software and AI.

As cigarette volumes decline, the group – which is also behind the John Player Special, Golden Virginia and Rizla brands – has been revamping its business, moving towards newer products including vapes, heated tobacco and oral nicotine.

It faces tax increases in Germany and a ban on the advertising of vaping and nicotine products in the UK from next June. Paravicini shrugged off the changes, saying the company had experienced regulation in other countries, and that sales of Blu vape products were growing at double-digit rates in the UK.

He added: “We support regulation on vapes, it will put more clarity in the market.”

The company’s total revenues fell 1.5% to £31.7bn in the year to 30 September. Profit before tax fell 12.1% to £2.7bn. Tobacco net revenues grew by 1.7% in key markets as the group raised its prices by 5.1%, which offset a 3.4% drop in volumes.
